hi Kally, this suggests to me that  you have a small data set and during the simulation a data set is generated with unstable MLE (not identifiable parameters).  You could resolve this possibly by weeding out the very extreme cases but I'm not going to recommend that approach.  Simplify the model might help too.
 
I'm not sure what nonparboot does.
 
regards
andy


 
On Fri, Aug 24, 2012 at 8:01 AM, kally <yuen....@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,

I have used parboot to obtain SE for a set of derived parameter estimates and one of them has resulted in a huge SE (estimate=0.77, SE=256).. Is there any way to avoid getting spurious values like this one?

Also, may I know the R commands for getting SE for these derived parameter estimates from nonparboot?

Thanks
Kally
